Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-09-24 | AAPL | Overweight | -1.7% | -1.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL, but earn the overweight rather than paying for it: keep the core untouched and put the first incremental tranche in at roughly one-third of the intended add — half as a limit at 328.00–330.00 (20 SMA 328.07 / VWMA 329.86 / −1 ATR 328.96) and half in at market on a hold of the 10 EMA at 334.16, so the desk does not repeat the 09-16 error of gating adds below a rising tape and never filling. Add the second third only on a daily close above 345.34 on ≥64M shares (retest preferred), move toward 1.15x standard only after that, and hold the final third until FQ4 confirms gross margin near/above 49.5% with inventory converting. Hard controls: tactical stop 319.50, trailing core stop 321.50, halt all new buying on a close below 328.07 on above-average volume, cut tactical exposure below 315.34; size on the 7.36% / 6.12% gap precedents (305–309), not on the 6.96 ATR, and consider a collar or puts for any above-standard exposure. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY26 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not genuinely contested; only price and size are — and on that split the aggressive seat wins the direction and the conservative and neutral seats win the sizing. That combination is Overweight, staged, not Buy at full size and certainly not Hold.

What the aggressive analyst established and nobody rebutted: the fundamental engine is accelerating, not bending. 9M FY26 revenue +16.2%, gross margin 49.07% (+225 bps), Q3 gross margin 50.06% — the first reading above 50% in this series — Q3 EPS +28.7% with growth stepping 18.3% → 21.8% → 28.7%, 9M operating cash flow $116,996M (+43.1%), FCF $110,197M (+52.5%) at a 30.2% margin, and $62,173M of net cash. The trend stack is intact and in correct bullish sequence (335.92 > 10 EMA 334.16 > 50 SMA 321.68 > 200 SMA 287.45), MACD remains above its signal, and the pullback to 335.92 on 24.7M shares — the lowest volume in 147 sessions, 58% of the 21-day average — is not distribution. VWMA has risen 21 consecutive sessions from 311.96 to 329.86. His reframing of the entry is also correct and decisive against the spot-based bear arithmetic: at 329 with a 319.50 stop the trade is ~1.7:1 to 345 and ~2.6:1 to 352.30, versus ~0.67:1 for buying 335.92. The conservative attack on 0.67:1 at spot was attacking an entry the plan does not take.

What the conservative analyst won, and why the add is not sized at 1.15–1.25x today: the headline reward-to-risk is gross, not net. Two single-session air pockets sit in this very window — −7.36% on 7/31 and −6.12% on 6/25 — so from 329 a tail event fills near 305, not 319.50; the stop is a level, not an exit. That is the one argument no seat answered, and it converts into a sizing rule rather than a veto. His momentum-decay evidence is real and shared by the neutral seat: MACD histogram 1.69 → 0.81, the 10 EMA's daily advance collapsing 1.49 → 0.39, RSI 66.9 → 61.3, and a marginal 345.34 high on lower MACD and RSI — a mild negative divergence inside one ATR of the 10 EMA. Valuation gives no cushion at ~36–37x run-rate EPS ($9.15), where 35x is ~320 and 40x is ~366, and the un-itemized ~$13.3B intangible against a ~$13.5B rise in other noncurrent liabilities, inventory +93.9% with raw materials +259.9%, R&D +32.5% against 16.2% revenue growth, and a 12% buyback decline are legitimate items to be confirmed by FQ4, not dismissed.

Where the conservative seat overreaches: it converts gap risk and pre-print uncertainty into a cap at standard weight and a demand for a 345.34 breakout plus retest before any real money. That is the posture this desk has already paid for repeatedly — 07-13, 07-20–07-24, 08-11–08-13, 08-17, 08-21, 08-24, 08-27, 08-28 and the 09-08 Underweight each forfeited multiple points of five-day alpha, while the 09-03 Hold (+2.4%), 09-04 (+5.3%), 09-09 (+6.5%) and 08-26 (+3.8%) Overweights paid. The 09-03 and 09-11 reflections name the error precisely: letting a strict confirmation stack or a pullback limit mechanically block participation in a confirmed uptrend. Refusing incremental capital to a 16.2% grower with 50.06% gross margin and a stacked 50/200 structure is a hidden bearish bet, not prudence — but so is paying above-benchmark size at %B near the upper band on an unconfirmed marginal high, which is why the 09-14 and 09-16 Overweights produced +1.8%/−0.1% and +1.4%/−0.7% (direction right, alpha nil) after sizing above benchmark into extended price.

The neutral construction governs, with one amendment drawn from our own losing record. Keep the BUY direction, make it conditional and smaller: no chase at 335.92; first tranche at one-third of the intended add, sized for a 7% gap toward 305–309 rather than a 2-ATR move; second third only on a close above 345.34 on ≥64M shares, preferably on a retest; third third held until FQ4 confirms gross margin near/above 49.5% with inventory converting and the intangible reconciled; target exposure moves toward standard first and only reaches 1.15–1.25x standard after price and fundamental confirmation. The amendment is the neutral seat's demand for a reversal confirmation inside 328–330 before the first tranche, which risks the exact non-fill that cost the 09-16 plan its entire thesis: with price at 335.92 and the 10 EMA at 334.16, a limit that only works if AAPL first trades 1.8% lower and prints a reversal is a coin flip against an intact uptrend. So half of tranche one goes in on a hold of the 10 EMA at market and half at the 328–330 confluence — the 09-16 reflection's instruction applied directly. Core exposure is never trimmed on entry-price discomfort alone (the 09-11 lesson); trimming is reserved for a close below 328.07 on above-average volume, and core reduction for a close below 315.34, which would invalidate the intermediate uptrend.

What would change the call: upgrade toward Buy on a daily close above 345.34 on ≥64M shares that holds a retest of 345/340, or an FQ4 print with gross margin ≥49.5%, inventory converting, buybacks re-accelerating against the 12% decline, and the ~$13.3B intangible explained. Downgrade toward Hold/Underweight on a close below 328.07 on above-average volume (halt all new buying, trim the tactical sleeve), a close below 319.50, then 315.34 with a negative MACD histogram, FQ4 gross margin below 48% without a one-time explanation, an inventory write-down, deteriorating China demand, or a quantified liability from the Apple–OpenAI/agent-liability or Siri matters. Stated gaps: no sentiment report this run (so sentiment is excluded as an input, not treated as supportive); no options chain or implied volatility, so the recommended puts/collar cannot be priced here; no segment, geographic or unit data, so 50.06% margin durability is unattributable on both sides; no FQ4 guidance or FY27 consensus to verify the multiple; no Q4 note on the intangible/liability build; and no portfolio context, so all sizing is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation and must respect their single-name limits.

**Price Target**: 345.34

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
Five-day alpha of −1.3% (raw −1.7%) marks the Overweight slightly negative, but against a 1–3 month horizon and a sizing frame built for a 7% gap toward 305–309 this window is too short to judge the thesis. It does undercut the choice to fill half of tranche one at market on the 10 EMA hold at 334.16 while MACD histogram was already decaying 1.69 → 0.81 and RSI 66.9 → 61.3, and it supports the conservative/neutral insistence on the 328–330 confluence and gap risk. Lesson for the next similar setup: when the confluence zone sits only ~1.8% below spot and momentum is diverging inside one ATR, invert the split — majority of the first tranche at the confluence, minority at market — rather than market-filling into the weaker tape.

[2026-09-23 | AAPL | Overweight | -1.2% | -0.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL. Build toward roughly 120–125% of a standard single-name allocation in staged tranches, but do not rely solely on the 329.5–333.8 limit zone that has repeatedly gone unfilled: initiate about 40% of the intended add now/into 333.8–337.0 (10 EMA to spot), completing at market if unfilled for roughly five sessions while price holds above 333.8. Add about 35% only on a daily close above 345.34 with volume above 50M shares, and keep about 25% for a held post-breakout retest or a 321.5–325 flush that does not break the 50 SMA. A close below 321.51 stops all adds and forces reassessment; a close below 309.1–309.4 cuts back to benchmark weight or below; size each tranche for gap risk, not just ATR risk.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction belongs to the bull; the entry and stop mechanics belong to the bear. That is why AAPL is Overweight rather than Buy or Hold.

The aggressive analyst wins the fundamental and primary-trend debate on evidence the conservative analyst never rebutted with numbers. Nine-month revenue is +16.1%, Q3 revenue +16.4%, so the re-acceleration is not a one-quarter fluke. Q3 gross margin reached 50.05% (+356bp) while cost of goods grew only +11.2%, which is the cleanest evidence of pricing power and mix. Nine-month FCF was $110.2B (+52.5%) at a 30.2% margin, net cash was $62.2B, up $28.4B, and debt fell $14.3B. The tape confirms the operating picture: the 50 SMA at 321.51 sits 11.96% above a rising 200 SMA at 287.16; the higher-low ladder 246.00 → 273.75 → 300.00 → 300.57 → 309.40 → 331.34 is unbroken; MACD is 6.208 versus a 5.005 signal with ten positive histogram sessions; RSI 62.90 is constructive, not stretched. The July gap-down has been absorbed. None of that supports Hold, and it specifically argues against repeating this desk’s pattern of under-owning AAPL inside an intact uptrend.

The conservative and neutral analysts win the near-term execution argument, and their points are real. At 337.02, upside to the 344.57–345.34 resistance cluster is only about 2.47%, while downside to the 50 SMA is about 4.60% and to the August base near 309.13 is about 8.27%. The 9/22 high of 345.34 pierced the upper band near 344.29 and closed back inside at 339.75, a band-tag rejection until proven otherwise. MACD peaked at 9.609 in July versus 6.208 at the higher September high, and volume has faded to 40.7M then 31.66M against a ~43.5M 20-session average, well below the 61–63M July breakout pace. The 326.90 tranche stop is also too tight: with ATR at 7.14, it is only about 0.4–1.0 ATR from a 331.50 entry and would be taken out by ordinary noise; the neutral analyst is right to treat it as a warning line, not the real risk boundary. And this name printed −6.12% and −7.36% single-day moves in the window, so gap risk must be controlled by tranche size and spacing, not by a close-in stop.

The bear’s fundamental flags are monitoring items, not thesis killers. Inventory +94% is concentrated in raw materials/purchased parts (+260%) while finished goods actually fell from $3.594B to $3.447B, and margins expanded at the same time; that is more consistent with strategic pre-buying than unsold devices. A 300bp gross-margin retracement would cost roughly $3.3B per year, but AAPL just banked +356bp in one quarter. Tax at 17.58% versus 15.39% and the 12% buyback cut are drags, not deterioration, given EPS still grew +22.4% and +28.7% in Q3. The valuation attack is the weakest bear leg: “36.7× annualized 9M EPS is a premium” is asserted without forward consensus EPS, peer multiples, or a comparable set. That is a mood, not a measurement.

The reason this is Overweight and not Buy is the entry geometry, plus the prior-lesson record. The 09-16 reflection is directly applicable: below-market add gates have repeatedly gone unfilled on a rising tape, so Tranche 1 should not be a passive 329.5–333.8 bid alone. I would initiate at the 10 EMA/spot area and treat the lower band as a bonus fill, not the only entry. The reason it is not Hold is that the business is accelerating, the trend is intact, and the 09-15 Underweight / 09-11 Hold record shows what excessive caution has cost when AAPL kept grinding higher. The conservative cap at benchmark weight is too restrictive for a 16% grower with expanding margins and $110.2B of nine-month FCF.

Risk lines for the whole position: a close below 321.51 means stop adding and reassess the September re-acceleration; a close below 309.1–309.4 breaks the higher-low sequence and cuts exposure back to benchmark or below. If the book is already at or above benchmark, keep the strategic core and use 344.5–345.3 only for optional trimming or hedging of a small trading sleeve.

What would change the call: downgrade before Tranche 2 if forward consensus or validated peer multiples show the 50%/mid-teens margin-growth assumption is materially wrong, if China memory-chip sourcing is quantified as a large margin hit, or if FQ4 gross margin falls below 48% with inventory building or a write-down. Upgrade toward Buy only on a daily close above 345.34 on more than 50M shares followed by a held retest, ideally confirmed by FQ4 gross margin at or above 49.5% with finished goods flat-to-down and the intangible/other-liability swing explained.

Stated gaps: no forward consensus EPS/revenue, no peer or historical multiple range, no confirmed dollar quantification of the China memory-chip story, no disclosure behind the +91% intangibles or +32.6% other non-current liabilities, and no portfolio context. All cited levels are technical, not valuation-derived. The Overweight is underwritten on demonstrated margin, growth, FCF, and trend structure—not on a valuation model.

**Price Target**: 345.34

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -0.5% (raw -1.2%) is mild underperformance, not a thesis test; five sessions is far too short to judge a 1–3 month Overweight call, and price never reached the 345.34 target or the 321.51 stop. The window mildly undercuts the near-term entry-geometry argument — initiating at the 10 EMA/spot area instead of waiting for the 329.5–333.8 zone bought into weakness rather than a confirmed hold above 333.8 — while leaving the fundamental case (16% revenue growth, 50% gross margin, $110.2B FCF, intact 50>200 SMA structure) untouched. Lesson: when the decision already concedes that upside to resistance is only ~2.5% and volume is fading, treat the first tranche as a probe sized for a pullback to the 50 SMA rather than a 40% commitment, and require a volume confirmation before the second tranche regardless of how long the bid goes unfilled.

[2026-09-22 | AAPL | Underweight | -3.0% | -1.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL at $339.75 — a tactical trim into resistance, not a franchise exit, and the sizing must reflect that distinction. Trim roughly 30–35% of the existing position with limit orders worked into the $340–$345 band (40–50% only if the position is oversized, levered, or cannot be monitored), initiate zero new money at spot, and retain roughly 65–70% of standard allocation as core. Tier the risk: $333.05 (10-EMA) is a close-only warning that pauses any rebuild, $328.85 (VWMA) triggers a further tactical reduction, and $321.06 (50-SMA) is medium-term invalidation opening $314.90/$309.90; rebuild only after stabilization, in small tranches, with a $320.50 stop, and restore to neutral-or-better only on a daily close above $345.34 on ≥60M shares with MACD >7.0 and RSI >70. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the September 22 Ternus/iPhone Duo event and the late-October FQ4 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not genuinely contested — all three risk seats, the Research Manager, and the trader converge on "trim into strength, keep a core." The dispute is magnitude (25–40% versus 40–50%), and that is what fixes the answer at Underweight rather than Sell. Sell means exit or avoid entry; nobody in this debate recommends that, and the aggressive analyst is right that holding 100% into poor near-term geometry is "inertia dressed up as patience," just as the conservative analyst is right that a name up 41% over twelve months at ~38x trailing earnings has little valuation cushion.

What decides the trim is location and the freshness of the rejection. AAPL tagged $345.34, pierced the upper Bollinger band at $344.29 by more than a point, and closed at $339.75 — the bottom 15% of a 6.59-point range — on 40.71M shares versus a ~43M average. The momentum work is tool-verified and not a sub-one-point artifact this time: MACD at 6.25 versus 9.45 at the identical July 28 price ($340.08) — roughly one-third less fuel to reach the same level — and RSI at 66.88 versus 68.90, having never printed above 70 anywhere in the 148-session dataset.
